headline: Alternative platforms rapidly absorbing institutional capital as regulated banks contract.

deltas.reads: Record AUM crossing $1.3T, driven by fee-earning and perpetual capital expansion in private credit, infrastructure, and insurance products.
Spread and fee-earning stack compounding through origination, retirement services, and insurance-backed platforms despite weaker exit environment.
Record fundraising and available capital, enabling large private-credit and alternative deployment independent of bank credit availability.

deltas.change: Raised $67B since prior quarter, including $44B insurance capital
deltas.reads: Insurance balance-sheet capital flowing into alternative platforms at scale, fulfilling regulatory-arbitrage pattern from bank constraints.
Even legacy active managers accelerating alternatives to escape fee pressure in traditional asset management, proving private-capital migration breadth.
Fee-paying AUM growth ($399.6B to $409.9B) and scale driving management-fee leverage, core to colonization thesis of higher fees replacing bank spreads.

momentum_note: Private capital colonization is accelerating across the data. Blackstone, Apollo, Ares, and Brookfield all show record or near-record capital scale, with alternative managers now absorbing tens of billions per quarter from institutions and insurance pools. Fee-generating AUM growth, perpetual capital expansion, and record available capital are outpacing realizations, proving that platforms are successfully converting former bank credit functions into higher-fee private capital channels. Franklin's alternatives surge to $294B confirms the trend extends across manager types. The regulatory arbitrage is structural: insurance balance-sheet capital and institutional outsourcing are flowing toward firms with fewer capital constraints and fatter fee structures.
